la:noun:via.html:
vĭa (vĕa, ), ae (
gen. sing. vias, Enn. ap. P., or Ann. v. 421 Vahl.; viāï, Enn. ap. , or Ann. v. 209 ib.; ; ; et saep.; dat. plur. VIEIS, Inscr. Lat. 206, 50), f.
Sanscr. vah-āmi, bring, lead; Gr. ὄχος, ὄχημα, vehicle; Germ. Wagen; Engl. wagon; from this root are also veho, vexo, etc.
, a way, in the most general sense (for men, beasts, or carriages, within or without a city), a highway, road, path, street.
Lit.
In gen.: viae latitudo ex lege duodecim tabularum in porrectum octo pedes habet, in anfractum, id est ubi flexum est, sedecim,: Romam in montibus positam et convallibus, non optimis viis, angustissimis semitis,: et modo quae fuerat semita, facta via est,: aut viam aut semitam monstret,: mi opsistere in viā,: ire in viā,: omnibus viis notis semitisque essedarios ex silvis emittebat, (opp. semita), ; ; cf.: decedam ego illi de viā,; cf. : paulum ad dexteram de viā declinavi,: decedere viā,: aestuosa et pulverulenta via,: quā (viā) Sequanis invitis propter angustias ire non poterant,: cursare huc illuc viā deterrimā,: in viam se dare,to set out on a journey,: te neque navigationi neque viae committere,: tu abi tuam viam,: milites monuit, viā omnes irent, nec deverti quemquam paterentur,along the highway,.—In a double sense: ire publicā viā,.—Prov.: qui sibi semitam non sapiunt, alteri monstrant viam, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 358 Vahl.): de viā in semitam degredi,: totā errare viā,.—
In partic., as the name of a particular street or road: tres ergo viae, a supero mari Flaminia, ab infero Aurelia, media Cassia,: Via Appia,; ; cf. ; v. Appius: Via Campana,; v. Campania: Sacra Via, in Rome, in the fourth region, Müll.; ib.; ; ; : Via Sacra,; also written as one word, SACRAVIA,; ; cf. P.; ib. (v. sacer, I. A.); cf. Becker, Antiq. 1, p. 219 sq.— Hence, Sacrăvĭenses, ĭum, m., those dwelling on the Sacra Via, Fest. s. v. October equus, p. 178 Müll.—
Transf.
Abstr., like our way, for march, journey (syn. iter): cum de viā languerem,: nisi de viā fessus esset,: tridui via, a three days' march or journey, : bidui,; : longitudo viae,: flecte viam velis,: tum via tuta maris,: feci Longa Pherecleā per freta puppe vias,: ne inter vias praeterbitamus, metuo,by the way, on the road,; ; Turp. ap. et saep.—
In gen., a way, passage, channel, pipe, etc.; thus, a lane in a camp, ; a passage between the seats of a theatre, ; ; of the veins: omnes ejus (sanguinis) viae,; of the chyle ducts: quaedam a medio intestino usque ad portas jecoris ductae et directae viae,; the windpipe, ; ; a cleft through which any thing penetrates, ; cf. ; the path or track of an arrow, ; a stripe in a party-colored fabric, et saep.—
Trop.
In gen., a way, method, mode, manner, fashion, etc., of doing any thing, course (cf. modus): vitae,; ; ; ; ; : via vivendi,: rectam vitae viam sequi,: Socrates hanc viam ad gloriam proximam dicebat esse,: haec ad aeternam gloriam via est,: haec una via omnibus ad salutem visa est,: invenire viam ad mortem,: totidem ad mortem viae sunt,: cum eum hortarer ut eam laudis viam rectissimam esse duceret,: haec est una via laudis, : totam ignoras viam gloriae,: quae tum promptissima mortis via, exsolvit venas,: habeo certam viam atque rationem, quā omnes illorum conatus investigare et consequi possim,: defensionis ratio viaque,, § 4: non tam justitiae quam litigandi tradunt vias,: docendi via,: optimarum artium vias tradere,: (di) non ... nullas dant vias nobis ad significationum scientiam,: rectam instas viam,i. e. you speak correctly, truly,.—Adverb.: rectā viā, directly: ut rectā viā rem narret ordine omnem,.—
Pregn. (cf. ratio), the right way, the true method, mode, or manner: ingressu'st viam, i. e. rectam,: in omnibus quae ratione docentur et viā, primum constituendum est, quid quidque sit, etc.,rationally and methodically,: ut ratione et viā procedat oratio,.—Adverb.: viā, rightly, properly (opp. to wandering out of the way): ipsus eam rem secum reputavit viā,: viā et arte dicere,. —
Viam perficere, i. e. to attain an end, proöem. 1.
